description: Package versions that entered the tree inside the 7-day maturity buffer, reviewed 7 and 14 days after publication (advisories, upstream issues, release notes), and dated milestones that ride the same list. Milestones are UTC dates derived from `published`. A review is recorded under `reviews.<milestone>` as { date, outcome: clean | flagged, note }, dated the day it is written and never later; one written up to 2 days before its milestone also carries early: { reason }, and the entry's later milestone stays due. A package entry leaves the list in the change that records its clean 14-day review; a date entry stays, with its `due` review recorded as the evidence that the day was reviewed, or, while what it waits for has not happened, its `due` moves forward with a dated `refs` line naming what was read; a package entry whose version leaves the tree before that review leaves the list too, because nothing is left to review. A date entry marks a contract milestone and never reviews a patched dependency: since 2026-10-15 every patch is watched by scripts/testing/patched-dependencies-gate.mjs, which reads the registry every 6 hours in the patched-dependencies workflow (fitness #48 holds its records), so the date entry patch-storybook-nextjs-vite-10.6.3 that ADR-0037 opened left the list the day the gate landed. A date entry never schedules a dependency move either: since 2026-10-14 (ADR-0036) a non-security bump is taken in the weekly Tuesday window and a toolchain lag is legal for 30 days, so the scheduled hold entries left the list, their evidence in the pull requests that took or retired each move. Read by scripts/testing/maturity-watchlist.mjs (--check in CI, --remind in the maturity-reminder workflow).

entries.title: Is there a jscpd release whose Rust build clears the seven crates.io advisories jscpd 5.4.2 still carries?
refs: Opened 2026-10-27 by the change that moved jscpd 5.4.1 → 5.4.2 and removed the jscpd@5.4.1 package entry, whose version left the tree: 5.4.2 clears RUSTSEC-2026-0346 to 0349 (its linux-x64-gnu binary names rustls-0.23.46 in its strings, 5.4.1's rustls-0.23.45), and one OSV batch over v5.4.2's rust/Cargo.lock (396 crates.io packages, read 2026-10-27T21:48Z) still returns RUSTSEC-2026-0367, 0368 and 0369 (zip 8.6.0, fixed in 9.0.0), RUSTSEC-2026-0374 (basic-toml 0.1.10, unmaintained), RUSTSEC-2026-0381 and 0383 (webpki-roots and webpki-root-certs 1.0.9, fixed in 1.0.10) and RUSTSEC-2026-0382 (rustls-webpki 0.103.15, CVE-2026-111943, fixed in 0.103.16). They are crates.io advisories inside an npm binary, so pnpm audit and the OSV npm query see none of them

Reachability, why the entry watches instead of blocking: rustls-webpki, webpki-roots and webpki-root-certs come in only through ureq in cpd-semantic and zip only through candle-core in cpd-semantic, the embeddings API and model downloads of --semantic, and basic-toml only through askama_derive, a compile-time macro of cpd-reporter. No script here passes --semantic: the only jscpd invocations are scripts/testing/jscpd-baseline-gate.mjs lines 117 (`apps/ packages/`) and 126 (`apps/ packages/ --baseline <scratch> --update-baseline --silent`), both reached by pnpm check:duplicates, and line 167 (`apps/ packages/ --update-baseline`), reached by check:duplicates:update-baseline (package.json); check:duplicates also runs in the CI step Duplicate code check (jscpd) in ci.yml and the battery step duplicates; .jscpd.json holds only absolute, baseline, failOnEmpty, failOnNewClones, format, ignore, minLines, minTokens, noTips and reporters, so no semantic, history or network option is set

Upstream, read 2026-10-27: master's b8c7deda (2026-10-21T06:38Z, 'fix(deps): update rustls-webpki and webpki-roots for the emSign advisories') moves rustls-webpki to 0.103.16 and webpki-roots and webpki-root-certs to 1.0.10, and #1230 drops basic-toml; no release carries them (v5.4.2, 2026-10-20T16:14Z, is the latest). zip stays at 8.6.0 on master, because candle-core 0.11 still needs zip 8, and upstream's cargo deny and cargo audit ignore 0367 to 0369 because jscpd extracts no archive (#1215, #1216)

The review, on the due date: read the npm registry for a jscpd release after 5.4.2 and, for each one, OSV-batch its rust/Cargo.lock at the release tag for the seven ids above; record which it clears, whether it is mature (7 days after publication), and what check:duplicates and a planted clone measure on it. A release that clears an advisory is a security-tied move, taken once mature with this entry's evidence; while none exists, `due` moves to the next Tuesday window with a dated line here. The entry stays until the tree's jscpd carries none of the seven, or until an advisory becomes reachable here, which is a move at once

Read 2026-11-05, two days after the 2026-11-03 due date (reminder #820): npm latest is still 5.4.2 (2026-10-20), so no release clears the seven advisories read on 2026-10-27, and no script or manifest passes `--semantic`; `due` moved from 2026-11-03 to 2026-11-10, the next Tuesday window.

entries.title: Does a distroless digest hold zlib1g 1:1.3.dfsg+really1.3.1-1+deb13u1 or later? When one does, take it and delete the zlib-patched stage of the four Dockerfiles
refs: docs/deployment/base-images.md, "zlib1g from Debian's archive on 2026-11-07": DSA-6613-1 fixes CVE-2026-85091, CVE-2026-76844 and CVE-2026-27171, and the images take that package from Debian's archive because no digest of the image held it. Container Security stays green while the stage stands, whether or not a digest has caught up, so this entry is what says when the stage can leave.

The read, each Tuesday: the `Version:` of `var/lib/dpkg/status.d/zlib1g` in the newest digest of `gcr.io/distroless/nodejs26-debian13` (`podman image mount`). A new digest alone proves nothing: `c952ca0a`, read 2026-11-07, carries Node 26.13.0 and the same `1:1.3.dfsg+really1.3.1-1+b1`. If a digest holds the fixed version or a later one, take that digest, delete the stage and its `COPY` from all four Dockerfiles, confirm Container Security stays green on the pull request, and delete this entry; if not, move `due` to the next Tuesday window.
